exposure: 6 mL of 1% lidocaine administered by epidural injection for breakthrough pain
6 mL of 0.15% ropivacaine administered by epidural injection for breakthrough pain
outcome: time for VAS scores decreasing to 3 or below
cervical dilation at the onset of first breakthrough pain
number of additional drug administrations during labor
VAS pain scores at various time points
postpartum hemorrhage within 2 hours after delivery
cohort: 120 obese primiparas experiencing breakthrough pain during the first stage of epidural labor analgesia at Nanjing Women and Children's Healthcare Hospital between October 2022 and December 2023.
finding: Both lidocaine and ropivacaine effectively suppressed breakthrough pain in obese parturients during epidural labor analgesia, but lidocaine demonstrated a shorter onset time and faster decrease in VAS pain scores.
mod_finding: There was no statistically significant difference in the mode of delivery between the lidocaine and ropivacaine groups.
